title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Procedures, Runbooks, and Comms Templates
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Comprehensive, production-grade on-call and incident response playbook covering incident lifecycle, roles, runbook patterns, postmortem process, rotation policy, game-day guidance, and status page / customer communication templates.
body:
Overview:

This playbook codifies Redwood Inference's standard incident lifecycle, on-call responsibilities, runbook structure, postmortem expectations, game-day exercises, and status page / customer communication templates. It is intended for SREs, platform, serving-runtime, and product engineers who participate in detection, mitigation, and post-incident analysis.

1) Incident taxonomy & severity levels

- Sev 1 (P0): Production outage affecting a majority of customers or causing failed requests for critical APIs (Redwood API / Dedicated control plane). Recovery objective: 0-30 minutes to mitigation; SLOs: restore user-visible traffic > 90% within 60 minutes.
- Sev 2 (P1): Major degradation impacting a subset of customers or significant latency/throughput regression. Recovery objective: 1-4 hours.
- Sev 3 (P2): Functional bug or minor degradation with workaround available. Recovery objective: next business day.
- Sev 4 (P3): Non-urgent operational tasks, maintenance, or docs updates.

For each severity, follow the Incident Process below and use the communication templates in Section 8.

2) Roles & responsibilities

- Pager (Primary on-call): Owns triage, initial mitigation, and incident timeline.
- Secondary on-call (Escalation): Provides deep expertise and supports the pager for 60+ minute incidents.
- Incident Commander (IC): Appointed for complex or multi-service incidents; coordinates cross-team work, prioritization, and customer comms.
- Scribe / Communicator: Maintains timeline, status updates, and publishes to status.redwood.ai.
- Engineering Owner: Service-specific owner who drives root cause and fixes post-incident.
- Postmortem lead: Author and owner of action items with due dates.

3) Incident process (step-by-step)

Detection & Alerting:
1. Alerts fire to #oncall-alerts with severity tag. Pager acknowledges within 5 minutes.
2. If no ack in 5 minutes, alert escalates to secondary and oncall-manager.

Triage (first 15 minutes):
1. Pager confirms scope (percentage of traffic affected, impacted regions, customer tiers).
2. Capture initial hypothesis, key metrics, and relevant runbooks.
3. If trending Sev1/Sev2, create incident channel (Slack channel: incident-<service>-YYYYMMDD).

Mitigation (15-60 minutes):
1. Run the service runbook checklist (see Section 4).
2. Apply short-term mitigation (scale up dedicated pools, failover to secondary region, rollback model or config).
3. IC decision: open customer-facing status or update existing status.

Recovery & Verification (60-240 minutes):
1. Verify customers see restored service for representative traffic.
2. Monitor 2× SLO window for regressions.
3. If recovered, transition incident to post-incident review.

Postmortem (within 72 hours):
1. Postmortem draft published to Confluence with timeline, root cause, and action items.
2. Assign owners and due dates.
3. Track action items in engineering backlog and review in weekly reliability sync.

4) Runbook pattern (standardized template)

Each service must maintain a runbook with the following top-level sections:
- Service name, owner, on-call rotation link, major dependencies.
- Key SLOs and alert thresholds.
- Observability dashboard links and relevant metrics (CPU/GPU utilization, 95th latency, request error rate, kvcache hit rate).
- Quick triage checklist (what to check first).
- Mitigation steps (ordered, reversible).
- Rollback procedure and safety checks.
- Post-incident cleanup and tickets to open.

Example runbook quick checklist for inference-api:
- Check ingress error rate > 1%? run: curl -s "https://monitoring/api?query=error_rate"
- Check model-serving node health: kubectl get pods -l app=model-serving -o wide
- If autoscaler is saturated: increase replica cap: kubectl patch hpa model-serving -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":40}}'
- If KV cache thrash: disable prefix cache for affected model: echo 'cache.disabled=true' > /etc/feature-flags/kvcache

5) On-call rotations & escalation policy

- Rotation cadence: 1 week primary on-call for platform and serving-runtime teams; 2-week rotation acceptable for low-volume teams with manager approval.
- Handover checklist: morning verification of alerts, outstanding incidents, and active tickets.
- Escalation timeline: 5 min to acknowledge, 15 min to escalate to secondary, 30-60 min to involve IC for unresolved Sev1s.
- Vacation and absence: use rotation-swap process documented in /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations.

6) Game days & training

- Quarterly game days coordinated by eng-sre. Objective: validate runbooks, test failover, and rehearse comms.
- Typical scenarios: control-plane partition, KV cache poisoning, cross-region outage, model regression at scale.
- After each game day produce a short report with at least 3 improvement items and owners.

7) Postmortem template & timelines

Required fields in every postmortem (must be non-nested strings in this document):
- Title, incident id, severity, timeline (bullet points with timestamps), summary, root cause, contributing factors, mitigation steps, detection timeline, customer impact, action items (owner + due date), lessons learned, and verification steps.

Postmortem deadlines:
- Draft within 72 hours of incident mitigation.
- Owner assigns action items within 7 days.
- Final postmortem published and reviewed in the weekly reliability meeting within 14 days.

8) Status page & customer communications templates

Use status.redwood.ai for all customer-facing updates. Templates below should be adapted and concise. Always include: what happened, who is affected, what we are doing, ETA for next update.

Initial public update (Sev1) — Title: Major outage affecting text generation API
We are currently investigating an incident affecting text generation requests in the US region. Some customers may see failed requests or increased latency. We have identified a subset of model-serving nodes exhibiting high error rates and are working to mitigate. Our engineers are actively working on a fix; next update in 30 minutes.

Customer guidance (Sev2) — Title: Degraded performance for embeddings endpoint
We are experiencing elevated latency for the embeddings endpoint for customers in EU-West. No data loss is expected. As a temporary mitigation, please retry requests and consider setting a lower concurrency. We are deploying a targeted autoscaler adjustment and will provide an update in 60 minutes.

Resolved update (all sevs) — Title: Incident resolved — text generation API
The issue affecting text generation in US has been mitigated. We restored service by failing over traffic to healthy model-serving pools and rolling back the recent quantization flag. We will publish a postmortem within 72 hours. If you continue to experience issues, contact support@redwood.ai.

Internal incident timeline sample (for postmortem):
- 09:03 — Pager alert: increased 5xxs for /v1/completions (US-west).
- 09:05 — Pager acknowledges, creates incident channel #incident-inference-20260304.
- 09:12 — Secondary escalated; identified KV cache thrash on model-x.
- 09:30 — Failover initiated to secondary region.
- 09:55 — Traffic stabilizes; monitor for 60m.

9) Tools, alert configuration, and SLOs

- Alerting targets: PagerDuty for P0/P1 with Slack integration to #oncall-alerts.
- Sample alert thresholds (service-level): error_rate > 1% sustained for 2 minutes (P1), p95 latency > 1.5× baseline for 5 minutes (P1), p99 latency spike > 3× baseline (P0).
- SLOs (example): request success rate >= 99.5% monthly, p95 latency < 300ms for small payloads. Maintain SLO burn rate dashboard and 3x burn-rate alert to the SRE oncall.

10) Metrics & dashboards to monitor

- Service overview: request rate, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, queue length, throttled requests.
- Model-level metrics: kvcache hit rate, kvcache eviction rate, attention cache size, token throughput.
- Alert links: Cloudwatch/Prometheus queries included in each runbook.

11) Ownership & contact list (example)

- Eng-SRE oncall rotation: #eng-sre-oncall (Slack).
- Incident commander rotation: eng-sre-rotation@redwood.ai.
- PagerDuty escalation policy: "Redwood P0 Policy".

Appendix A — Runbook checklist (copyable)

- [ ] Confirm alert details and scope.
- [ ] Create incident channel and add stakeholders.
- [ ] Triage root cause signals and metrics.
- [ ] Apply short-term mitigation steps.
- [ ] Communicate status to customers.
- [ ] Verify recovery and monitor.
- [ ] Draft postmortem and assign action items.

Appendix B — Communications snippets (for Slack/email/internal)

Internal short update:
- We are investigating increased 5xx errors for /v1/completions in US-west. Working on mitigation; next update in 15 minutes.

Escalation request (to product/CS):
- Heads up: Sev1 impacting text generation for multiple customers. IC requested product on standby for customer comms.

Closing notes:

This document is the canonical on-call and incident response playbook. Runbook owners should keep service-specific runbooks up-to-date and link them here. Game-days and runbook reviews should be scheduled quarterly. Questions or proposed changes: file a PR on the confluence page and ping eng-sre@redwood.ai for review.
